name: Amman
tagline: Ancient History, Warm Hospitality, and Surprising Affordability
description: Amman is a sprawling, hilly capital that bridges the ancient and modern Middle East. Built over Roman ruins and Nabataean trade routes, the city offers affordable living, excellent Arabic cuisine, warm Jordanian hospitality, and proximity to bucket-list sites like Petra, the Dead Sea, and Wadi Rum. Healthcare is strong and affordable by Western standards, and English is widely spoken in educated circles. While summers are hot and the city lacks coastal access, Amman rewards curious retirees with deep cultural richness and genuine value.

quickFacts.visa: Visa on arrival for US citizens (single entry); Jordan Pass includes visa and site entry
quickFacts.safetyRating: High – one of the safest capitals in the Middle East
quickFacts.climate: Arid Mediterranean with hot dry summers and cool wet winters

housing.description: Small furnished 1BR/studio in a safe, unpretentious hillside area (Jabal Al-Weibdeh / Tla' al-Ali)

dining.description: Falafel/shawarma/mansaf from local spots, mostly home cooking

healthcare.description: Basic individual private cover (expats can't use the public system)

1M.lifestyle: A frugal but genuinely livable Amman rhythm — a small furnished flat on one of the older, greener hillsides like Jabal Al-Weibdeh, meals built around falafel, shawarma, and mansaf from neighborhood spots with home cooking in between, and Careem rides instead of a car. Basic private cover keeps the well-regarded hospitals in reach. There is little slack for travel, but the Roman citadel, Rainbow Street cafés, and Dead Sea day trips cost almost nothing.

housing.description: Modern 3BR apartment in Abdoun, Deir Ghbar, or a villa flat in Dabouq with views

dining.description: Regular dining at Amman's best restaurants, mezze feasts, rooftop dinners, cafe culture

healthcare.description: Premium private insurance with access to top hospitals like Jordan Hospital and Khalidi

transportation.description: Own car for Dead Sea and desert trips; taxis for daily city use

entertainment.description: Petra weekends, Wadi Rum camping, Dead Sea spa days, cultural events, gym membership

2M.lifestyle: A comfortable step up — a nicer furnished flat on the edge of Weibdeh or Sweifieh, dining out a couple of times a week, and a better individual health plan. Heavier ride-hailing with the occasional rental car for weekend escapes, plus a gym and regular café life. Amman feels relaxed and affordable here, with room for a modest travel habit.

housing.description: Good furnished 1BR or compact 2BR in a prime district (Sweifieh/Abdoun)

transportation.description: Own car: fuel + insurance + maintenance amortized

entertainment.description: Gym, cinema, social life, weekend trips

3M.lifestyle: A genuinely comfortable Amman life with real margin — a good furnished flat in a prime district like Abdoun, regular dinners at the city's better restaurants, and a car for Dead Sea and desert escapes. Premium health cover brings specialist access. Weekend flights to Cairo, Beirut, or Istanbul are easy, and the monthly cushion is comfortable rather than tight.

housing.description: Grand villa in Abdoun or Dabouq with swimming pool, garden, and panoramic city views

dining.description: Personal chef for daily meals and entertaining, exclusive dining experiences, imported wines

healthcare.description: VIP private healthcare with international hospital network access and medical evacuation

transportation.description: Luxury SUV, second vehicle, full-time driver, first-class flights from Amman

entertainment.description: Private archaeological tours, luxury desert expeditions, Red Sea diving in Aqaba, cultural patronage

domesticHelp.description: Full-time housekeeper, cook, gardener, and security; live-in domestic help is affordable

luxuryExtras.description: First-class regional travel, luxury Dead Sea property access, antiquities study, philanthropy

5M.lifestyle: An upscale Amman lifestyle — a luxury flat or small villa in Abdoun or Deir Ghbar, near-daily dining out, and part-time household help a few times a week. A nicer car, a strong regional health plan, and a generous entertainment-and-travel budget. Amman's modest costs mean this level of comfort still leaves a wide margin each month.

housing.description: Prime villa or large luxury residence in Abdoun/Dabouq with grounds

transportation.description: Luxury car + fuel (driver folded into household staff)

domesticHelp.description: Near-full-time housekeeper + part-time cook/driver (not estate staff)

10M.lifestyle: The ceiling of Amman living — a prime villa in Abdoun or Dabouq with grounds and a pool, near-daily fine dining, and near-full-time household staff. International, evacuation-grade health cover, a luxury car, and an uncapped discretionary and travel budget. Amman's small, affordable market caps how much can be spent here without waste, so this is a lavish life that still costs a fraction of the same in a global capital.
